title: release: one-time npm dist-tag sweep for the pre-release tags that 18.1.0 left stale (maintainer-run)
body:
Filing-gate category: ① a measured, user-visible defect on a public entry (the npm registry), the one-time half of #25581. Maintainer-directed: Tesla ruled on 2026-10-25 (director thread) that the manual cleanup gets its own maintainer-owned card instead of waiting for the next stable release.

Maintainer-action: once #26196 has landed (it teaches `scripts/release-dist-tags.mjs` to **remove** the retired `rc` tag rather than move it), run `node scripts/release-dist-tags.mjs` (plan) and then `node scripts/release-dist-tags.mjs --apply` from a checkout of `main`, logged in to npm with an account that holds publish rights on `@objectstack`. It is done when `npm view @objectstack/spec dist-tags` shows **only `latest` and `next`**, with `next` at the newest stable or above, and the planning run reports 0 tags would change. (Rescoped 2026-10-26 on the maintainer's 「现在只有 latest 和 next」 / 「同意」: `rc` is removed, not moved. The original line had `next` and `rc` both moved to `18.1.0` or above.)

## What a user sees

Measured on the registry at 2026-10-25 09:10Z, identically for the 73 published packages of the fixed group:

```
{ "rc": "17.0.0-rc.6", "next": "18.0.0-next.5", "latest": "18.1.0" }
```

`npx create-objectstack@next` or `npm i @objectstack/cli@next` installs 18.0.0-next.5, a pre-release of a version already two stable releases behind `latest`; `@rc` is a whole major behind. The plan run of the sweep script reports 141 tag moves (next and rc on each of 73 packages → 18.1.0), 0 kept, 0 skipped.

## Why a maintainer, and why a card

- #25691 (merged 2026-10-24 23:19Z, closes #25581) wired the sweep into release.yml's `publish` job, but 18.1.0 published at 09:19Z the same day, before the step existed, so the stale tags stay until the next stable publish.
- The script writes through the npm CLI with whatever login is configured; no seat holds npm publish rights and no fleet token may be used for it (#25691 header: "⛔ Not run by any agent with any token"). Only a holder of the `@objectstack` publish rights can do it.
- This card exists so the action is tracked and verified rather than remembered: it sits in `pm:awaiting-maintainer`, is never dispatched, and the director seat removes the label with an evidence comment once the dist-tags read back correct.

## Not in scope

- No workflow_dispatch lane for the sweep (declined in #25691 for maintenance-cost reasons).
- If the next stable release publishes first, its post-publish step performs the same moves; the verification above still closes this card.

Business rationale: an evaluator or an AI agent that picks `@next` today receives already-fixed bugs as current ones; the fix is a two-minute action by the one person who can do it.
